SM Moonir, Advocate ----- For the Petitioners.

parties:
Daulatpur Ice Cold Storage Ltd and another ------ Petitioners
vs
Chairman Power Development Board and others ------ Respondents
full_judgment: 10. It appears that on the detection of pilferage by the respondents, the respondents filed Criminal Case No. 249 of 1994 before the learned Magistrate, Power Development Board, Khulna Zone, Khulna, wherein the respondents claimed that the petitioners pilfered 91,200 units of electric energy and the petitioners admitted the claim without any question and accordingly, the learned Magistrate convicted the petitioner Nos. 2 and 3 others for the said offence and fined each of them to pay an amount of Taka 10,000 each and also directed the Power Development Board to prepare a bill for 91,200 units along with compensation. In due course the petitioner No.2 and the other accused’s deposited the fine amount and the petitioners requested the respondents for issuance of the bill in terms of the Judgment of the learned Magistrate. The respondents did not submit any bill, instead they issued a notice for disconnecting the electric line and ultimately demanded an inflated bill of Taka 50 lac and odd whereupon the petitioners obtained the instant Rule. It appears that in compliance of the court's order the petitioners have already paid the required amount for 91,200 units and an affidavit of compliance has also been filed before this court showing payment of Taka 6,84,000 being price for 91,200 KWH. In view of the order passed by the Appellate Board on 15-6-1997 which has been quoted in paragraph No. 12 of the affidavit-in-reply dated 1st of June, 1999, it appears that the impugned claim of Taka 50 lac and odd is, in fact, inflated and baseless. It appears that the judgment passed by the learned Magistrate in Complaint Case No. 249 of 1994 has not been challenged by the Power Development Board and, as such, now they cannot claim any amount beyond 91,200 KWH because it appears from Annexure 'C' to the application that after making an assessment of pilferage they claimed that amount which was duly accepted by the learned Magistrate. Thus, the claim of Taka 50 lac and odd made by the respondents vide bill dated 18-10-1994 is illegal and without jurisdiction and not tenable in law. Here it may not be out of place to mention that the Power Development Board cannot claim any arrear amount beyond 3 years from the date of consumption of electricity which is the general limitation provided by the law of limitation, Since the petitioners have already paid 6,84,000 for 91,200 units, there remains nothing for them to pay any more on that count.
